I’m Henry, a software and AI engineer based in Lagos, Nigeria. My research interests are artificial intelligence, machine learning, and natural language processing. I have a background in Computer Science Education at Tai Solarin University of Education (TASUED, class of 2026), alongside a strong foundation in frontend and backend engineering.

I build scalable software systems, from user-facing interfaces to backend services, and work comfortably with AI workflow tools. I contributed to building QwamPay as part of a team, working on backend systems and AI-assisted financial operations. I also built LeAi as a personal project to help students learn from their own course materials.

I enjoy research, analytical thinking, and working collaboratively to solve problems. Consistent personal development is central to how I work: I keep learning, refine my technical skills, and apply what I learn through practical projects. I want to bring that approach into graduate research and contribute to a team studying intelligent systems.

Manuscript in preparation2026

Time-Series AI-Driven Congestion Management in Enterprise Campus Networks: A Simulation Using Cisco Packet Tracer and REST APIs

Henry Oderinde · Final-year project

Combining network telemetry and an LSTM model to predict congestion and inform routing and quality-of-service decisions in a simulated campus network.

Project details

The project connects a Cisco Packet Tracer controller to a Node.js / Express service through REST APIs. An LSTM model uses telemetry observations to classify congestion, with model output informing OSPF cost and QoS recommendations.

The project used 17,280 telemetry observations and reported 93.22% classification accuracy. Full evaluation details will accompany the manuscript.

Manuscript and full paper not yet publicly available.

Personal project · AI for education

Full Stack AI Engineer · LeAi

I built LeAi to help students prepare for exams using the materials they already have. It turns PDFs, documents, slides, and scanned notes into grounded practice assessments through retrieval-augmented generation and OCR.

10,000+ students served · Developed through four product iterations and CcHUB incubation.

My contribution

I used Python for backend processing and retrieval algorithms, including the OCR, prompt, and data pipelines. I built the frontend with React and TypeScript for interactive study workflows and typed application code. I launched the first version in a month and led product iterations. Caching and removing redundant calls reduced server requests by about 90% during a launch-day traffic surge.
